name: Chicken gizzards
summary: Tender chicken gizzards simmered in a spicy curry, tomato and green pepper gravy, the township favourite for mopping up with pap.
about: Gizzards are one of the most loved cheap cuts in South African townships, sold from taxi-rank stands and shisanyamas and cooked at home on a budget. They need a slow boil to turn tender, then a fry in onion, curry and tomato to make a thick, spicy gravy. Pap is the natural partner, with chakalaka or a salad on the side.
steps: Rinse the gizzards and trim off any tough yellow skin or fat. Put them in a pot with the water, salt and bay leaves, bring to the boil over high heat, then cover and simmer over low heat for 50–60 minutes, until a knife goes in easily. Drain, keeping 1 cup of the cooking water.
Cut any large gizzards in half. Heat the oil in a wide pot or deep pan over medium heat and fry the onions and green pepper, stirring, until soft and starting to brown, about 8 minutes.
Add the garlic, ginger, curry powder, paprika and chilli and stir for 1 minute until fragrant, adding a splash of the cooking water if the spices start to stick.
Add the gizzards and fry for 3–4 minutes, stirring, until they are coated and lightly browned.

Add the tomatoes, stock cube and the reserved cup of cooking water. Bring to a simmer, then cook uncovered over low heat for 15–20 minutes, stirring now and then, until the gravy is thick and glossy and clings to the gizzards.
Taste and season with pepper and more salt if needed, scatter with coriander or parsley and serve hot with stiff pap or rice.
prepNote: Boil the gizzards the day before and keep them in the fridge; the finished dish keeps 2 days.
